claims.text: Reducing surface defect density decreases the binding strength of oxygenated intermediates on nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Weaker binding of oxygenated intermediates enhances catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
As-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have an inherent distribution of surface defects.
A controlled post-synthesis thermal annealing treatment can reduce surface defect density without inducing phase segregation or significant compositional change.
The PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution phase is thermodynamically stable within the proposed ethanol-oxidation operating conditions.
Surface defect density and local atomic coordination influence the adsorption strength of oxygenated intermediates.
Thermal annealing produces a more uniform local atomic arrangement.
The more uniform local atomic environment weakens adsorption of poisoning oxygenated intermediates.
Weaker adsorption of poisoning oxygenated intermediates prevents catalytic-site blockage.
Preventing site blockage improves catalyst durability while sustaining ethanol-oxidation activity.
Annealed catalysts will have lower coverage of strongly adsorbed oxygenated intermediates than untreated catalysts under identical ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Annealed catalysts will retain stable activity for longer than untreated catalysts.
Untreated catalysts maintain a higher surface-defect density than annealed catalysts.
Surface defects in untreated catalysts promote stronger binding of oxygenated intermediates.
The proposed mechanism applies only where annealing primarily changes surface defects rather than causing phase segregation or material degradation.

contradictions.description: The material is consistently written as PtPdRhRuIrOs, which contains six elements, but the boundary calls it a quinary solid-solution catalyst.
